categories.main_business_segments: Duke Energy operates two primary reportable business segments: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure (EU&I) and Gas Utilities and Infrastructure (GU&I). EU&I includes regulated electric utilities in the Carolinas, Florida, the Midwest, and related transmission infrastructure. GU&I comprises regulated natural gas local distribution companies and related storage, pipeline, and renewable natural gas investments. The company also reports 'Other' for non-core activities, including holding company costs and captive insurance.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Duke Energy's core operations rely on large-scale electric power generation (nuclear, natural gas, coal, hydro, and renewables), transmission, and distribution infrastructure, as well as natural gas distribution networks. The company utilizes advanced grid technologies, smart meters, and digital platforms for operational efficiency and customer engagement. Nuclear fuel processing, coal ash management, and grid modernization (including self-healing and undergrounding) are key technical areas.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal users of electricity and natural gas within regulated service territories. Major end markets include households, businesses, manufacturers, and wholesale buyers such as municipalities and electric cooperatives. The company also serves power generators and participates in wholesale energy markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Duke Energy's regulated electric and gas utilities serve approximately 8.2 million electric and 1.6 million gas customers across six U.S. states: North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio, and Kentucky, with some gas operations in Tennessee. The company’s service territory covers about 92,000 square miles and a population of 26 million, primarily in the Southeast and Midwest.
categories.supply_chain_position: Duke Energy operates primarily as a downstream utility, delivering electricity and natural gas directly to end users. It owns and operates generation assets (upstream/midstream for electricity), transmission and distribution networks (midstream/downstream), and natural gas distribution infrastructure (downstream). The company also has some midstream investments in pipelines and storage.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Duke Energy's strategic focus is on a clean energy transition, targeting net-zero carbon emissions from electricity generation by 2050 and significant methane reductions in gas operations. Key initiatives include retiring coal plants, expanding renewables and energy storage, modernizing the grid, and investing in advanced nuclear, hydrogen, and long-duration storage technologies. The company is also pursuing digital transformation, customer experience enhancements, and regulatory modernization.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through regulated sales of electricity and natural gas to retail and wholesale customers, with rates set by state and federal regulators to recover costs and provide a reasonable return on investment. Additional revenue streams include transmission and distribution charges, riders for specific investments, and limited nonregulated activities.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Duke Energy is one of the largest regulated utilities in the U.S., operating as the sole provider of electricity and/or gas in most of its service territories, except for competitive generation supply in Ohio. Its main competitors are other regional utilities, merchant generators, and alternative energy providers, especially in wholesale markets and in response to distributed generation and energy efficiency trends. The company is a market leader in its core regions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For 2022, Duke Energy reported total operating revenues of $28.8 billion and net income attributable to common shareholders of $2.44 billion. The company has a large asset base ($178 billion total assets at year-end 2022) and a capital expenditure plan exceeding $12 billion annually. Growth is driven by ongoing investments in grid modernization, clean energy, and customer growth in its regulated territories, with a stable dividend track record (96 consecutive years).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Duke Energy emphasizes reliable, affordable, and increasingly clean energy delivery, leveraging its scale, diverse generation mix, and regulatory relationships. Its value proposition centers on operational excellence, customer service, and leadership in the clean energy transition, including ambitious carbon and methane reduction goals. The company differentiates itself through its integrated utility model, strong regulatory framework, and commitment to innovation and sustainability.
